(2/9) Insurance

IRDAI proposed tighter expense and commission limits.

That put PB Fintech and life insurers under pressure.

At the same time, insurance demand has improved after GST removal on individual life and health policies.

Five years after famous tech apps hit the stock market, everyday investors are paying more than Rs 200 for every Re 1 of profit they generate.  

On paper, they celebrate finally turning profitable. But look at where that cash actually came from

Zomato (Eternal): Made Rs 366 crore in final profit, but earned nearly Rs 1400 crore just sitting on bank interest and treasury cash.

Policybazaar (PB Fintech): More than half its profit came from interest on idle cash, not selling insurance.

Paytm (One97): Made Rs 552 crore in profit, while over Rs 850 crore was non operating interest income.  

Their apps have millions of daily users but the actual core business is barely breaking even.

PB FINTECH TO IRDAI: THE PROPOSED LIMITS DON’T REFLECT HOW ONLINE INSURANCE REALLY WORKS

More importantly, PB Fintech says that if the proposed limits are implemented in their current form, they may not fully reflect the operational and servicing cost structure of online insurance distribution.

Why?

Policybazaar says its model involves substantial spending on consumer education, digital onboarding, pre-sale advisory and end-to-end claims assistance, particularly in Health and Term Insurance.

In other words, PB Fintech is effectively telling the regulator: online insurance distribution has a cost structure that needs to be recognised while setting commission and distribution-expense limits.

The company says it is evaluating the impact and will submit detailed feedback and representations to IRDAI.

IRDAI PROPOSES CHANGES TO INSURANCE DISTRIBUTION

📊 **Major falls on 24 September 2026**

🔻 **PB Fintech** — **−36.0%**

🔻 **ICICI Prudential Life** — **−3.4%**

### WHY DID THE MARKET REACT?

IRDAI proposed changes involving:

• Lower Expense of Management limits
• Product/segment-specific commission limits
• Greater disclosure of distributor remuneration
• Stronger safeguards against mis-selling
• Restrictions on certain digital “dark patterns”
• Changes to insurance distribution structures

📌 **Important:** These are **proposals under consultation — NOT final regulations**. Stakeholder comments are invited until **25 October 2026**.

PB Fintech (Policy Bazar) 

 stock falls 36% in a day ....

Reason: 

IRDAI has proposed tighter limits on the commission insurance platforms like Policy bazar that can earn from selling policies → this one policy change will affect future earnings of the company. 

Suppose if I have invested in this stock, I don't blindly average down just because a stock is cheaper. 

A falling price is not always an opportunity, 
Sometimes, it's gives a warning signal. 

In this case, economics of the business have changed and that may impact the future earnings. 

So don't confuse a falling stock with a cheap stock. 

Sometimes the price falls because the market is overreacting.

Sometimes it's falls because the business economics have changed.

Figure out which one it is...

My End of Q1FY27 Analysis Summary [Part 2]

​Continuing my sector-wise watchlist tracking. 

Focusing on businesses with high growth, margin expansion, and strong commentary.

​1] Auto & EV Space

1.1)​Ather Energy: 

Moving fast from loss to profit. Their new mass-market scooter expands the customer base beyond premium buyers. Capacity is doubling by Q3 due to strong demand, and their software subscription attach rate is a massive 93%.

​1.2)Mahindra & Mahindra: 

The clear winner in the 4-wheeler SUV trend. Consumer preference is fully shifted to SUVs and M&M is capturing it perfectly

1.3)​Ola Electric: 

On my wait-and-watch list. Need to track how their new dealership model and in-house battery cell manufacturing perform before taking a view.

​2] Dairy Sector 

2.1)​Milky Mist: 

A pure value-added product (VAP) player. They don't sell low-margin raw milk, so they avoid seasonal dips. Focused entirely on high-margin paneer, cheese, and high-protein foods, easily growing at 30-40% through deep distribution.

​3] Hotels & Hospitality

3.1)​Leela Palaces: 

Operating entirely in the ultra-luxury segment. Despite global travel issues, their domestic business grew 25-30% in Q1 without them having to drop room rates to fill beds. Planning aggressive expansion from 4,000 to 10,000 rooms by FY30.

​4] Logistics

​4.1)Shadowfax: 

Taking market share in the fast-growing express delivery space. They recently turned profitable and confidently upgraded their growth guidance from 30% to 40%.
The only monitorable is their high dependence on Meesho.

4.2)​Shiprocket: 

Asset-light platform model. The core shipping business is doing well, and new segments like warehousing are driving revenue, though still at a loss. Note that Q3 is usually weak for them as D2C brands shift to Flipkart/Amazon for festive sales.

​5] Alcohol Beverages 

5.1)​Piccadily Agro: 

A pure premiumization story. Their 'Indri' single malt is a massive hit. They are spinning off their low-margin sugar business next year to become a pure luxury alcohol play, guiding for 60% to 70% growth.

5.2)​Radico Khaitan: 

Steadily moving away from mass-market liquor into high-margin premium brands (like Rampur), which is naturally expanding their operating margins.

​6] Pharma (Oncology & CDMO)

6.1)​Sakar Healthcare:

Heavily focused on the fast-growing Oncology space, aiming to take it from 30% to 70% of total revenue. Partnered with Intas for European distribution and guiding for 35% top-line growth.

​6.2)Shilpa Medicare:

Getting strong approvals in highly regulated markets for high-margin biosimilars.

6.3)​OneSource: 

Massively expanding capacity (from 20,000 to 1.5 lakh) to manufacture high-demand GLP-1 weight loss injections for export markets.

6.4)​Kwality Pharma:

 Another strong Oncology player that just upgraded its revenue guidance to ₹700 Cr.

Pharma Sector needs vigorous tracking just like every other Sector!

सोचिए एक ही झटके में किसी कंपनी के शेयर 36% तक ज़मीन पर आ गिरें! बड़े-बड़े बैंक, दिग्गज इंश्योरेंस कंपनियाँ और करोड़ों की फंडिंग वाले फिनटेक जायंट्स सन्नाटे में आ जाएं... आखिर ऐसा क्या ला दिया देश के बीमा रेगुलेटर IRDAI ने?"

"क्या यह आपकी जेब के लिए खुशखबरी है? या फिर लाखों एजेंटों और बैंकों की कमाई का 'गेम ओवर'?
चलिए विस्तार से समझते है …'इन्श्योरेंस का नया नियम: राहत या आफत?'"

भारतीय बीमा विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण (IRDAI) ने सितंबर 2026 में बीमा वितरण, कमीशन और बिक्री के तरीकों में भारी सुधार के लिए एक ड्राफ्ट जारी किया है। इसी प्रस्ताव को लेकर देश के बीमा और वित्तीय बाजार में बड़ा बवाल और हलचल मची हुई है।

इस प्रस्ताव का सबसे सीधा असर बीमा बेचने वाले बैंकों, ऑनलाइन एग्रीगेटर प्लेटफॉर्म्स (जैसे PolicyBazaar), NBFCs और एजेंट्स की कमाई पर पड़ने की आशंका है।

शेयर बाजार में गिरावट
IRDAI का यह ड्राफ्ट सामने आते ही शेयर बाजार में इंश्योरेंस और फिनटेक कंपनियों के शेयरों में भारी गिरावट देखने को मिली…

 PolicyBazaar (PB Fintech) के शेयर एक ही दिन में रिकॉर्ड 36% तक गिर गए।
 Max Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential और SBI जैसी प्रमुख बीमा कंपनियों व बैंकों के शेयरों पर भी बुरा असर पड़ा।
 
ब्रोकरेज फर्म्स और विश्लेषकों का मानना है कि यदि यह प्रस्ताव लागू होता है, तो इंश्योरेंस डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर्स और बैंकों की कमीशन से होने वाली आय घट जाएगी।

दरअसल IRDAI ने पॉलिसीधारकों के हितों की रक्षा और गलत तरीके से पॉलिसी बेचने (Mis-selling) को रोकने के लिए कई सख्त प्रस्ताव रखे हैं…

कमीशन पर दोबारा कैप (सीमा) लगाना:
 वर्ष 2023 में IRDAI ने कमीशन की सीमा हटा दी थी, जिसे अब दोबारा लागू करने का प्रस्ताव है।

 पहले वर्ष में मिलने वाले भारी-भरकम कमीशन (जो कई मामलों में 40% या उससे अधिक होता था) को घटाकर उत्पादों के हिसाब से 5% से 20-25% के दायरे में लाने का सुझाव है।

एजेंट/एजेंसी को बड़ा एकमुश्त कमीशन देने के बजाय कमीशन को पॉलिसी की पूरी अवधि (Tenure) में बांटकर देने की बात कही गई है।
￼￼
बैंकाश्योरेंस (बैंकों द्वारा बीमा बिक्री) और लोन-लिंक्ड बीमा पर सख्ती:
बैंक अक्सर ग्राहकों को लोन देते समय जबरन बीमा पॉलिसी खरीदने के लिए दबाव बनाते थे। 

IRDAI ने इस पर रोक लगाने और ग्राहक को किसी भी कंपनी से पॉलिसी चुनने की आजादी देने का प्रस्ताव दिया है।

मल्टी-ब्रांड बेचने वाले बैंकों और कॉर्पोरेट ब्रोकरों के लिए कमीशन की दरें और कम रखी गई हैं।

मोटर इंश्योरेंस (गाड़ियों के बीमा) में बदलाव:
नए वाहनों के अनिवार्य 'थर्ड-पार्टी मोटर बीमा' पर कॉर्पोरेट डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर्स को 0% कमीशन और एजेंट्स को केवल 2.5% देने का प्रस्ताव है।

डिजिटल 'डार्क पैटर्न्स' पर प्रतिबंध:
ऑनलाइन ऐप्स/वेबसाइट्स पर ग्राहकों से बुनियादी जानकारी दिखाने से पहले उनकी निजी डिटेल (फ़ोन नंबर/ईमेल) मांगने पर रोक लगाने का सुझाव है।

बीमा का मूल्य और नियम पारदर्शी रूप से बिना नंबर मांगे दिखाए जाने चाहिए।

मिस-सेलिंग की जवाबदेही (Policy Tagging):
हर बेची गई पॉलिसी को बेचने वाले एजेंट या प्रतिनिधि से डिजिटल रूप से 'टैग' किया जाएगा, ताकि मिस-सेलिंग होने पर जवाबदेही तय की जा सके।

IRDAI ने यह कदम क्यों उठाया?
लागत में भारी बढ़ोतरी: IRDAI के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, वित्तीय वर्ष 2024-25 में बीमा कंपनियों ने ₹60,800 करोड़ कमीशन के रूप में बांटे (18% की वृद्धि), जबकि बीमा प्रीमियम में बढ़ोतरी सिर्फ 6.73% ही हुई।

उपभोक्ताओं को लाभ: कमीशन और वितरण लागत कम होने से बीमा पॉलिसियां सस्ती होंगी और प्रीमियम की दरें घट सकती हैं।

आम जनता पर इसका क्या असर होगा?
आम उपभोक्ताओं के लिए यह प्रस्ताव बेहद फायदेमंद साबित हो सकता है। मिस-सेलिंग रुकेगी, पॉलिसी की दरें (प्रीमियम) सस्ती होंगी और बैंक लोन लेते समय जबरन बीमा नहीं थोप सकेंगे।
 
 नुकसान (एजेंट्स/एजेंसियों के लिए): बीमा एजेंटों, डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म्स और बैंकों की फीस/कमीशन से होने वाली कमाई पर सीधी चोट पहुंचेगी।

वर्तमान स्थिति: यह अभी एक ड्राफ्ट (प्रस्ताव) है, जिस पर IRDAI ने सभी पक्षों (कंपनियों, एजेंट्स और जनता) से सुझाव मांगे हैं। अंतिम नियम लागू होने से पहले इनमें कुछ बदलाव या संशोधन की संभावना बनी हुई है।

IDEA Weekly | Indian Equities

𝗪𝗲𝗲𝗸 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝟮𝟱 𝗦𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲

Indian equities closed lower for a seventh consecutive week. Nifty 50 fell 0.9%, Nifty 500 1.0%, Nifty Bank 1.4%, Nifty Midcap 100 2.1% and Nifty Smallcap 100 0.9%. The deeper signal remains breadth. Only 40% of the tracked universe was above its 200 day average, while 146 stocks made 52 week highs against 187 lows. FIIs sold Rs 11,490 Cr during the week, while DIIs bought Rs 16,398 Cr, helping contain index damage despite weaker internals. Crude remained above USD 100, US yields stayed elevated and the rupee hovered near 95.8 against the dollar. The market is not seeing indiscriminate selling, but participation is narrowing and domestic liquidity is doing more of the heavy lifting.

𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗰𝗸𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗼𝘂𝘁

PB Fintech / Insurance: IRDAI's draft proposals could materially reset insurance distribution economics. PB Fintech management's initial assessment suggests general insurance revenue could reduce by one third to 40% if implemented in the present form, while life economics appear less affected. The 36% fall was therefore not merely sentiment. The market was repricing the economics of the business model itself.

#PBFintech #Insurance

Waaree Energies: the 2 GW module order adds FY27 and FY28 visibility, but given Waaree's existing scale, the more interesting development may be its entry into specialty gases for solar cell and semiconductor manufacturing. That moves the story from capacity expansion within solar towards capturing more of the manufacturing value chain.

#WaareeEnergies #Renewables

Welspun Corp: its largest ever HFIW pipe order, worth around Rs 4,000 Cr, takes the global order book to a record Rs 45,000 Cr. More importantly, execution is scheduled across FY28 and FY29. This is less about an immediate FY27 earnings boost and more about extending revenue visibility further out than the market usually gets with industrial businesses.

#WelspunCorp #EnergyInfrastructure

Dr Lal PathLabs: the Rs 168 Cr acquisition of 70% in SN Genelab implies an upfront valuation of around Rs 240 Cr for a business that generated Rs 57.96 Cr revenue in FY26. The strategic question is therefore not size, but whether Dr Lal can use its network and customer base to scale higher value genomics materially faster.

#DrLalPathLabs #Diagnostics

Balaji Amines: commercial production has started at the expanded acetonitrile plant, taking capacity to 1,440 tonnes per month, or 17,280 tonnes annualised. The investment case now moves from capex completion to monetisation. Utilisation, realisations and the resulting operating leverage matter far more from here than the capacity announcement itself.

#BalajiAmines #SpecialtyChemicals

𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗸

Visibility was repriced in both directions this week. Regulation reduced visibility for insurance distributors, Welspun extended it into FY29, Waaree added new growth adjacencies, Balaji moved from capex to utilisation and Dr Lal bought a capability it now needs to scale. In a weaker market, execution is increasingly worth more than optionality.

India Weekly Market Review

September 21–25, 2026

Indian equities extended their losing streak to a seventh consecutive week. The Nifty 50 fell 0.88% to 23,140.50, while the Sensex declined 0.53% to 73,895.74. The Nifty has now fallen about 5.8% across seven straight weeks, its longest such losing run since the Covid-era sell-off. 

Sector performance

SectorWeekly move

Nifty Realty+3.0%
Nifty Consumer Durables+1.1%
Nifty Pharma+1.1%
Nifty FMCG+1.0%
Nifty India Defence+0.5%
Nifty Metal+0.3%
Nifty Oil & Gas-0.8%
Nifty Auto-0.6%
Nifty Private Bank-1.5%
Nifty IT-2.4%

The rotation was notable. Realty rebounded almost 3%, while pharma, consumer durables and FMCG held up relatively well. IT was the weakest major sector, followed by private banks and energy. 

Stock movers

The sharpest midcap sell-off came in PB Fintech, which plunged 33.1% for the week after IRDAI proposed changes to insurance-distribution economics. The proposed commission and expense changes raised concerns about the future earnings model of insurance intermediaries. 

Paytm and Oracle Financial Services Software each fell about 9.5%, while L&T Finance declined 9.2% and Container Corporation fell 8.5%. 

At the other end, Patanjali Foods gained about 10.1%, Mankind Pharma 7.6%, ICICI Lombard 6.6%, Phoenix Mills 5.4% and SAIL 4.3%. The moves were largely stock-specific rather than driven by a single broad market catalyst. 

Engineers India was another standout, gaining strongly after announcing a $450 million Dangote Group contract to provide project-management and EPCM services for a 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery and petrochemical project in Kenya. 

Welspun Corp also attracted attention after its US subsidiary won a $412.5 million HFIW pipe order, its largest such order, reinforcing the company's US infrastructure exposure. 

The macro backdrop

The week's biggest macro variables were oil, US yields and foreign flows.

Brent crude initially surged above $100 as Middle East tensions intensified, but prices subsequently fell sharply as hopes of renewed US-Iran negotiations and improved oil-flow conditions emerged. Brent ended the week around $97–98. 

The bigger pressure came from global bonds. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.19%, its highest level in years, keeping pressure on emerging-market assets and particularly rate-sensitive Indian equities. India's 10-year government bond yield also remained elevated. 

The Federal Reserve had raised rates to 3.75–4.00% the previous week, while its projections continued to leave the door open to another increase. The combination of higher US yields and a firm dollar remained a major headwind for foreign flows. 

The Bank of Japan also raised its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18, its highest level in 31 years. The move added another element to the global monetary-tightening story and reduced the attractiveness of Japan as an ultra-cheap funding source. 

The rupee, however, was relatively stable, ending at ₹95.82/$ versus ₹95.87 the previous Friday. 

Foreign investors remained the major source of selling pressure. FIIs sold ₹11,490 crore during the week, while DIIs bought ₹16,398 crore, providing a significant counterweight. 

The Mercator Take

The important development this week was not simply another fall in the Nifty. It was the continued divergence beneath the index.

Global liquidity remains tight, US yields are above 5%, foreign investors continue to withdraw capital and geopolitical uncertainty is keeping oil volatile. That combination is weighing disproportionately on IT, financials and other rate-sensitive areas.

Yet domestic liquidity is preventing a disorderly decline, while selected domestic sectors and company-specific stories are attracting buying interest.

Bottom line:

India's position isn't shifting from a complete “no” to an unrestricted “yes.”

It's moving towards a conditional model: approved investment, local manufacturing and strategic safeguards.

This also connects to India's bigger industrial push.

Critical minerals supply the battery materials.

Semiconductors support vehicle electronics.

Auto PLI encourages domestic manufacturing.

The real opportunity lies in connecting these policies into one functioning supply chain.

Now consider the opportunity for Indian component makers.

More local EV manufacturing can create demand for batteries, motors, power electronics and specialised components.

Technology partnerships may help build capabilities that would otherwise take years to develop.

But incentives alone won't guarantee localisation.

But here's the important distinction.

Allowing Chinese investment doesn't automatically mean giving Chinese companies control.

India's approach remains focused on FDI approval, security checks and local manufacturing.

The objective is to access technology without creating fresh strategic vulnerabilities.

And India already has an example of this model.

JSW MG Motor India combines JSW Group with China's SAIC.

Tata AutoComp also has Chinese partnerships in EV drivetrains and automotive air-conditioning systems.

Such ventures show how Indian manufacturing and foreign technology can work together.

Think of two very different situations.

A Chinese company imports finished EVs into India.

Or it invests in an Indian factory, brings technology and builds a local supply chain.

The second creates manufacturing opportunities, but also raises questions around ownership and strategic dependence.

That's where the policy shift comes in.

On September 23, an official indicated that existing auto PLI applications involving Chinese investment may be considered if FDI approval is already in place.

India wants to manufacture more EVs locally.

But China has deep expertise in batteries, motors and power electronics.

Building a competitive EV ecosystem takes more than assembling cars.

It also requires access to the technology and components inside them.

First, why was the door closed?

Since 2020, investments from countries sharing India's land borders have required government approval.

BYD's proposed ~$1 billion EV factory was blocked, while Great Wall Motor's India plans stalled.

But India's EV ambitions created a difficult question.

India said no to Chinese carmakers. Now, the door is opening.

After years of blocking major Chinese auto investments, India may allow some Chinese-backed companies to access its Rs.25,938 crore auto PLI scheme.

What changed? And who stands to benefit? 👇

Start with NBFCs. Insurance commission income now eats into profit before tax at levels that should worry anyone tracking these stocks.

Poonawalla Fincorp sits at 17.8%, Cholamandalam at 16.3%. Even HDB Financial, M&M Financial, and CreditAccess Grameen hover around 13%.

If the cap forces a 50% cut in this income, L&T Finance alone could lose roughly 13% of its PBT.

Now look at banks through a slightly different lens, bancassurance income as a share of total fee income for FY26. Bandhan Bank tops the list at 26.4%, way ahead of everyone else. HDFC Bank pulls in ₹6,927 crore from this, 16.9% of its fee income. Axis Bank is at 15.1%, IndusInd at 15.5%, Yes Bank at 14.9%. 

Private banks as a group get 12.4% of fee income from bancassurance, more than double the PSU bank average of 6%. Foreign banks land in between at 8.6%, largely driven by Standard Chartered at 13.6%.

That's why analysts specifically called out Axis Bank and HDFC Bank as more exposed among private lenders, simply because fee income and PBT lean harder on this line for them than for peers.

Then there's the second table, insurance commission as % of PBT for specific financiers. L&T Finance again leads at 0.26, more than triple Poonawalla Fincorp's 0.18. The Legend of Willy Jeep , From Toledo to the Indian Army  🚙

#IndianArmy #WillysJeep #MilitaryHistory #ADGPI 

📌The Willys MB (and the almost identical Ford GPW) was built in the United States in 1941 as a light reconnaissance vehicle: about a quarter-ton, four-wheel drive, a 60 hp “Go-Devil” engine, and a body that could be repaired with a spanner in a ditch. Allied commanders later ranked it among the tools that mattered most in the Second World War. General George C. Marshall called it “America’s greatest contribution to modern warfare.” War correspondent Ernie Pyle wrote that it went everywhere and was “as faithful as a dog, as strong as a mule and as agile as a goat.

📌Jeeps reached 🇮🇳 during the Burma  🇲🇲 and Kohima campaigns. After 1947 they stayed. Mahindra & Mahindra won a licence to assemble Willys kits and later built the high-bonnet CJ-3B, the machine most Indians still mean when they say “Willys” or “army jeep.” The Indian Army used these jeeps (and later the Nissan Jonga) into the 1980s as command cars, ambulances, and, crucially, mounts for the 106 mm recoilless rifle

📌The story that turned the jeep into legend is the Battle of Asal Uttar (8–10 September 1965), in the Khem Karan sector of Punjab — the largest tank battle in the subcontinent since the Second World War.

📌Jarpal Queen (1971). 3 Grenadiers captured a Pakistani Willys jeep at Jarpal in the Shakargarh sector. Once fitted with a recoilless gun, it still carries Urdu markings. The regiment keeps it running, has used it on guards of honour,

📌Moral of the Willy Jeep:
You don’t need to look expensive to change a battle. You just need four-wheel drive, a gun mount, and a driver who treats “impossible” as a suggestion.

Timex Group India beyond Q1 FY27 numbers

Timex Group India is not just about Timex watches. It has a portfolio across price points with Timex, Guess, Versace, Ferragamo, Nautica, Philipp Plein, Furla and newer brands like Aston Martin. It manufactures and assembles watches in India and sells through e-commerce, 5000+ multi-brand outlets, large format stores, its own retail network and luxury retail.

The scale up has been sharp. Revenue has moved from ₹422 Cr in FY24 to ₹540 Cr in FY25 and ₹801 Cr in FY26. More importantly, EBITDA margin expanded from 8.3% to 9.2% to 14.5% over the same period.

Q1 FY27 continued this trend with total income of ₹219 Cr, up 30%, EBITDA of ₹35.8 Cr, up 63%, EBITDA margin of 16.3% vs 13%, and PBT of ₹33.8 Cr, up 70%. Timex and Guess led brand growth, Aston Martin was among the fastest growing brands, while e-commerce and trade led channel growth.

The Baddi plant produced around 4 million watches last year and capacity has already been increased to 6 million. This gives Timex room to grow volumes without immediately adding another large manufacturing setup.

The opportunity is coming from multiple directions; growth of the core Timex brand, scaling Guess and other premium brands, adding newer brands, e-commerce and getting more sales through an already large distribution network.

One unusual development has been promoter holding falling from 74.93% to exactly 51% through two OFSs. The global parent has monetised a large part of its holding but continues to retain majority control. It has consequently also increased the public float substantially.

The gaps are mainly around disclosure. Timex does not conduct concalls, so it is difficult to get brand wise revenue, volume vs pricing growth, ASP trends, brand level margins or detailed forward guidance. Royalty and advertising costs also need to be watched.

The numbers to follow now are revenue growth and margins. If 25% to 30% sales growth continues with EBITDA margins sustaining around 15% to 16%, operating leverage can keep earnings growth well ahead of revenue growth.

🚨 IT STOCKS UNDER PRESSURE FOR 6TH STRAIGHT SESSION: NIFTY IT DOWN 4% IN 6 DAYS

Indian IT stocks extended their decline on September 25, with rising US bond yields, crude oil above $100 and concerns around global technology spending keeping the sector under pressure.

🔹 Nifty IT: down ~0.6% at 10:30 AM
🔹 6-session decline: over 4%
🔹 Infosys: down ~2%
🔹 TCS: down ~0.5%
🔹 OFSS: down ~5%
🔹 Nifty IT remained the weakest sectoral index

Only a handful of IT names, including HCLTech, LTM and Persistent Systems, were trading in positive territory during the morning session.

WHY ARE IT STOCKS FALLING? 👀

The biggest macro concern is the renewed rise in US interest-rate expectations.

Crude oil above $100 has intensified global inflation worries, while comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers have strengthened expectations that additional rate hikes may be required.

Higher US rates can potentially slow economic activity and discretionary technology spending, an important factor for Indian IT companies because of their significant exposure to the US market.

INFOSYS UNDER PRESSURE 📉

Infosys fell around 2% today after already losing roughly 5% over the previous five sessions.

The sector continues to face questions around:

🔹 Weak discretionary technology spending
🔹 Higher-for-longer US interest rates
🔹 AI-led pricing disruption
🔹 Pressure on traditional IT-services models
🔹 Near-term earnings growth

OFSS HAS AN ADDITIONAL PROBLEM ⚠️

Oracle Financial Services Software fell around 5%, making it one of the biggest losers in the broader market.

Its US parent Oracle fell more than 3% overnight after reports that it invoked force majeure relating to the massive Project Jupiter AI data-centre development in New Mexico because of potential power-related delays.

However, OFSS has separately clarified that it is a distinct listed entity and has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The current IT correction isn't being driven by a single factor.

Higher US rates + expensive crude + cautious global tech spending + AI disruption concerns are collectively putting pressure on sector sentiment.

The Nifty IT's six-session decline of more than 4% shows that investors are again reassessing growth expectations for Indian technology companies.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

The upcoming September-quarter earnings season becomes particularly important.

Management commentary on discretionary spending, large-deal wins, AI-related revenue, pricing, margins and FY27 growth expectations could determine whether the current weakness remains primarily macro-driven or starts showing up materially in earnings.

For now, Indian IT remains caught between the long-term AI opportunity and the near-term risks of higher rates, slower global spending and disruption to traditional services.

🚨 OFSS FALLS OVER 5%: ORACLE TRIGGERS 'FORCE MAJEURE' ON MASSIVE AI DATA CENTRE PROJECT

Oracle Financial Services Software (OFSS) shares came under heavy pressure again after its US parent Oracle issued a force majeure notice linked to Project Jupiter, a massive AI data-centre campus in New Mexico.

🔹 OFSS intraday fall: over 5%
🔹 Intraday low: ₹10,332
🔹 Lowest level in over 9 weeks
🔹 Trading volumes jumped sharply
🔹 Oracle shares also fell in the US
🔹 Project Jupiter targeted to come online in 2028

WHAT HAPPENED? 👀

Oracle issued a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit developing Project Jupiter, citing potential delays in securing adequate power for the facility.

The notice does not mean Oracle is exiting the project.

According to reports, Oracle is seeking contractual protection that could allow it to delay certain payments if the data centre is delayed and fails to become operational on schedule.

POWER IS THE BIG ISSUE ⚡

Project Jupiter is designed to handle around 2.45 GW of capacity, making reliable energy infrastructure critical.

A natural-gas pipeline intended to support the site has reportedly been delayed by nearly six months, while other permitting issues around the project's power infrastructure remain unresolved.

The project is part of the massive AI infrastructure build-out associated with Oracle and OpenAI.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The development highlights one of the biggest challenges emerging from the global AI boom:

AI demand may be enormous, but building enough data centres, power generation and grid infrastructure fast enough is becoming increasingly difficult.

However, an important distinction is necessary for OFSS investors.

OFSS has previously clarified to the exchanges that it is a separate listed entity from Oracle and said it has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

Therefore, the current OFSS price reaction is primarily linked to sentiment around its parent Oracle rather than a disclosed operational impact on OFSS itself.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

Oracle has said Project Jupiter remains on schedule and that it remains fully committed to the New Mexico project. Blue Owl has also said the notice does not change the parties' financial commitments.

The key monitorables are now power availability, permits, the 2028 commissioning timeline and any changes to financing or contractual obligations.

For OFSS specifically, the crucial question is whether parent-level AI infrastructure concerns remain only a sentiment overhang or eventually have any measurable impact on the Indian listed company's fundamentals.

JSW Group wants Volkswagen to cover a $1.4 billion local tax liability — a key unresolved issue in the proposed tie-up

JSW has indicated it would not proceed if it had to assume the tax burden

Treatment of the possible large tax bill among the outstanding issues that could affect the deal

Final valuation remains under discussion as financial due diligence begins

Two sides targeting a binding agreement by December

The Deal Structure
Involves JSW making an investment in closely held Skoda Auto Volkswagen India

JSW seeking a majority stake

Proposed venture would develop, build and market passenger vehicles in India and for export

Covering internal-combustion engines, battery-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and hybrids

Preliminary agreement reached on joint venture structure and other commercial terms

Why VW Needs This Deal
VW has spent nearly two years looking for a local partner in India to share costs and risks — after talks with Mahindra & Mahindra broke down

German automaker aims to crack India's vast, fast-growing car market

Holds only a token share through its Skoda Auto unit despite substantial investment in local manufacturing and development of dedicated models over past two decades

Part of broader turnaround strategy — counting on India to help pull it out of a prolonged slump

The Tax Issue
Stems from Indian government's allegation that VW misclassified some vehicle assembly kits imported from Germany, Czech Republic and Hungary between 2012 and 2024

Misclassification allegedly reduced the levies VW had to pay — a claim VW has denied

VW challenging the tax demand before a court in Mumbai

Resolution unlikely before end of the year

JSW executives' position: any liability arising from the case pending before Indian courts should remain with the German automaker

ಮಂಗಳೂರಿನ ನೀರಿನ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗೆ ಪರಿಹಾರ: ತುಂಬೆ ಡ್ಯಾಮ್ ಎತ್ತರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಸಮುದ್ರದ ನೀರು ಶುದ್ಧೀಕರಿಸಿ – ಕಾಮತ್
ಮಂಗಳೂರು: ನಗರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕುಡಿಯುವ ನೀರಿನ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ತೀವ್ರವಾಗುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆ ಹಿನ್ನೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತುಂಬೆ ಡ್ಯಾಮ್‌ನ ನೀರು ಸಂಗ್ರಹ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮಂಗಳೂರು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ಶಾಸಕ ಡಿ. ವೇದವ್ಯಾಸ ಕಾಮತ್ ವಿಧಾನಸಭೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮನವಿ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ.

ಬರಗಾಲದ ಕುರಿತು ನಡೆದ ಚರ್ಚೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತನಾಡಿದ ಅವರು, ತುಂಬೆ ಡ್ಯಾಮ್‌ನ ಎತ್ತರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವುದರಿಂದ ಮಂಗಳೂರು ನಗರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ನೀರು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಲು ಅನುಕೂಲವಾಗಲಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದರು. ಡ್ಯಾಮ್ ಎತ್ತರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವ ವೇಳೆ ಮುಳುಗಡೆಯಾಗಬಹುದಾದ ಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳ ಜನರಿಗೆ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಪರಿಹಾರ ನೀಡಬೇಕು ಎಂದರು.

ಇದರ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಪೂರೈಸಲು ಸಮುದ್ರದ ನೀರನ್ನು ಶುದ್ಧೀಕರಿಸುವ ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ಯೋಜನೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸುವಂತೆ ಸರ್ಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಸಲಹೆ ನೀಡಿದರು. ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ಎಂಆರ್‌ಪಿಎಲ್ ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ 20 ಎಂಎಲ್‌ಡಿ ನೀರನ್ನು ಇದೇ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಕಾಮತ್ ತಿಳಿಸಿದರು.

野党の意見を収斂させるとも、集約するとも申しておりません。副次的にそれが起きるにせよ、最大の目的は「野党の存在自体の収斂」です。

「野党が大きな塊を作ることにつながる選挙制度とし、自民党(に限らず特定政党)が比較第1党であり続けやすい状況を打破せねばならない」と申しています。

少数政党が多く並び立つことは、小さな民意の「議席」への反映や、国政の場でそれらが問題提起されることには繋がります。

他方、自民党の比較第1党、自民党を中心とした政権樹立の蓋然性を高めることにも繋がり、結果として、それを前提として社会構造が決し、「現状維持微修正」のレベルの中で許容される変革しか起き得ぬ状況をも生んでいます。

私はその状況の方に問題意識を強く覚えます。

「小さな民意」が、そのまま議席となるのではなく、「収斂」「集約」の対象となってしまうとしても、実際に権力に基づいてそれらが(完璧、完全な形でないにせよ)社会実装され得る社会を、私は望みます。

The global auto landscape is undergoing a massive realignment.

Chinese EV makers are dismantling Europe’s home turf, and legacy Western giants are scrambling for cover in India.

Here’s how the battlefield is shifting:

1. Europe’s Fortress is Cracking
BYD, MG, and Chery are outpricing European OEMs on their own soil. Even with EU tariffs, a 25–30% Chinese cost advantage, vertical battery control, and software-first cockpits are driving German margins into the red and triggering plant shutdown warnings.

2. The India Trade Dynamic: Europe vs. China
• India–EU FTA push: Europe wants steep cuts on imported car duties (CBUs/CKDs). India’s response? Phased cuts tied to local manufacturing commitments ($500M+ capex, ~50% domestic value addition).
• The China reality: No FTA on the table. With Press Note 3 restricting direct FDI, Chinese EV tech can enter India mainly through local JVs and alliances (e.g., JSW–MG).

3. Home Turf Defense
Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra aren't blinking. They own the mass-to-mid EV space with localized supply chains, dealer dominance, and aggressive price points. European brands sit at barely ~2% Indian market share; they can't survive on imported models.

4. The Volkswagen Playbook & The JSW Stumbling Block
VW needs an Indian giant to build affordable platforms and split capital costs. It signed a non-binding MoU with JSW for a 51:49 JV, with a binding deal targeted by year-end.
The catch? A disputed ~$1.4B (₹11,526 Cr) customs notice hanging over VW/Skoda for allegedly classifying imported kits as parts instead of CKDs. JSW has drawn a hard line: VW must ring-fence and absorb the entire tax liability before any binding deal is signed.

The Bottom Line:
The road to surviving the EV transition runs straight through deep localization, not import duty workarounds. If legacy giants can't crack local alliances in markets like India, they risk getting squeezed from both ends.

Raw material choice decides the process, the price, the customer, and the demand cycle for any pipe.

Plastic / polymer pipes
Made from PVC, CPVC and similar resins. Used in agriculture, bathroom plumbing and sub-soil water lines.  
Key players: Supreme Industries, Astral, Finolex, Prince, Apollo Pipes, Ashirvad, Prakash Pipes.

Stainless steel pipes
Steel alloyed with nickel and chromium for corrosion resistance. Used in food processing, dairy, pharma, chemicals and railings. Higher cost, so specified only where ordinary steel would rust and fail.

Carbon steel pipes
Made from ordinary steel. This is the largest category.

Carbon steel pipes split into three types by manufacturing process:

Ductile Iron (DI) pipes — cast from pig iron. Main use: drinking-water pipelines under Jal Jeevan Mission. Players: Rashmi Group, Jindal SAW, Electrosteel, Jai Balaji.

Seamless pipes — no welded joint, so they handle very high pressure. Used in oil & gas drilling, boilers and defence. Players: Maharashtra Seamless, ISMT, Jindal SAW, Ratnamani.

Welded pipes — a flat steel coil is rolled into a tube and the seam is welded. This is the biggest segment. It further divides into large-diameter LSAW/HSAW pipes (oil & gas trunk lines) and ERW pipes (Electric Resistance Welded), the most common type for general use.
Players: APL Apollo, Tata Tubes, Welspun (ERW line), Sambhav Steel Tubes, etc

Large-diameter LSAW/HSAW players: Man Industries (India) Ltd, Welspun Corp, Jindal SAW.

Research Note: #PBFintechLimited (#Policybazaar)

1. Company Overview
PB Fintech Ltd (NSE: #POLICYBZR ) is India’s largest online insurance and credit marketplace. Its flagship platforms are:
- #Policybazaar – Insurance comparison & distribution (core business)
- #Paisabazaar ** – Credit marketplace (personal loans, credit cards, etc.)
- #PBPartners – Tech-enabled network of independent agents/advisors (offline reach into Bharat)
- Newer verticals: Corporate insurance, Reinsurance broking, PB UAE, Pensionbazaar, PB Wheels, Account Aggregator (PB Money)

Mission: Help the Indian middle class deal with Death, Disease and Disability (the 3Ds).

As of June 2026:
- 158.9 million registered consumers
- 28.1 million transacting consumers
- 71.6 million policies sold till date

2. Business Model & Unit Economics
Revenue Streams:
- Commissions / brokerage from insurers on new business
- High-margin renewal / trail income (sticky, ~80% margins)
- Credit marketplace fees
- New initiatives (PB Partners, Corporate, UAE, etc.)

Key Strengths:
- Dominant online market share (>90% of online insurance policies sold historically)
- Strong shift toward **protection products** (Health + Term) — now >70% of core online revenue
- Renewal ARR has compounded strongly (₹935 Cr in FY26, ~80% margins)
- Asset-light model with high operating leverage once scale is achieved

3. Financial Performance Snapshot
 Full Year (April 2025 – March 2026)
The company made ₹6,794 crore in total revenue. This is 37% higher than the previous year.
Insurance business grew strongly — total premium collected reached ₹29,934 crore (up 42%).
Profit almost doubled to ₹670 crore.
The company is now clearly profitable and margins are improving.

Latest Quarter (April – June 2026)
Revenue: ₹1,888 crore (up 40% from the same quarter last year).
Insurance premium: ₹8,372 crore (up 41%).
Profit: ₹163 crore (almost double compared to last year).
Profit margin improved from 6% to 9%.

Highlights:
- Profitability turned consistently positive from FY24 onwards.
- Management is on track for ~₹1,000 Cr PAT in FY27.
- Contribution margins in core online business remain healthy (~42–44%).
- Loan disbursals (Paisabazaar) also growing well (₹30,740 Cr in FY26; +33% in Q1 FY27 core online).

4. Segment Insights

#Policybazaar (Core Online):
- Health insurance market share of 
fresh retail business has risen sharply to ~18–20% (from ~4.5% in FY22).
- Protection products driving quality growth.
- Renewal income is the compounding engine.

PB Partners:
- Expanding rapidly into Tier 2–5 cities via 450k+ partners.
- Market share gains visible; lead over next player widening.

#Paisabazaar :
- Recovering and turning EBITDA positive.
- Expanding into mutual funds & bonds.

International (UAE):
- Became profitable in FY26; premium growth strong (~54% YoY).

5. Competitive Landscape
#Policybazaar remains the clear leader in digital insurance distribution in India. Key competitors include:
- InsuranceDekho (post RenewBuy merger — stronger challenger)
- Turtlemint
- Coverfox / others

Digital still forms a small portion of overall Indian insurance distribution (traditional agency + bancassurance dominate). This leaves significant runway if digital penetration rises.

6. Growth Drivers
1. Under-penetration of insurance in India (especially protection products).
2. Rising health insurance awareness + GST benefits earlier.
3. Shift from pure comparison to full-stack “phygital” (digital + offline partners).
4. High-margin renewals compounding.
5. Credit marketplace recovery + cross-sell.
6. New initiatives (Corporate, Reinsurance, UAE, Pension, etc.) providing optionality.

Management guidance: Sustain ~30% premium growth trajectory.

🚨 INSURANCE STOCKS ARE FALLING 🚨

“ HERE’S WHAT JUST HAPPENED” 

If you saw Policybazaar, insurers, banks & NBFC stocks falling today, this is the simple reason 👇

IRDAI has proposed a major change in how insurance is sold and how much distributors can earn.

⚠️ Important: These are proposals, NOT final rules yet.
Comments are open until 25 October 2026, with implementation expected from FY28 through a phased approach.

🧵 WHAT IS IRDAI TRYING TO CHANGE?

Think of it like this:

Today, insurance distributors can earn significant commissions for selling policies.

IRDAI is basically saying:

“Insurance should be sold because customers need it, not simply because the distributor earns a lot by pushing it.”

The regulator wants to reduce excessive commissions, improve transparency and make insurance more affordable and sustainable.

💰 1. LOWER EXPENSE LIMITS

IRDAI is proposing tighter limits on how much insurers can spend.

For life insurers:

➡️ Around 15% of gross direct premium in 2 years

➡️ Around 12.5% in 5 years

➡️ Some already-efficient insurers could move toward 10%

For general insurers:

➡️ Around 20% in 5 years

In simple words:

Insurers may have less room to spend heavily on commissions, distribution and other expenses.

💸 2. COMMISSIONS COULD COME DOWN

This is the part the market is worried about most.

IRDAI wants to bring back product- and channel-specific commission limits.

Instead of paying a huge amount upfront for selling a policy, payouts could be:

➡️ Lower in the first year

➡️ Spread across the policy period

➡️ More closely linked to the actual effort/service involved

This could particularly affect:

🔹 Term insurance
🔹 Health insurance
🔹 Motor insurance
🔹 Credit-linked insurance

🏦 3. BIG CHANGE FOR BANKS & NBFCs

One proposal could have a major impact:

Banks/NBFCs would not be allowed to compulsorily bundle insurance with loans.

For example:

You take a ₹50 lakh loan.

The bank cannot effectively say:

“Take this insurance policy along with the loan.”

And credit-linked insurance commissions could become as low as 2–5% in some cases.

That is potentially a big change from the economics of these products today.

🚨 4. MIS-SELLING WILL GET MORE EXPENSIVE

IRDAI also wants:

✅ Stronger anti-mis-selling rules
✅ Commission clawbacks
✅ More disclosure of commissions on large policies
✅ Restrictions on “dark patterns”
✅ Less volume-based pressure on bank employees
✅ Simpler distributor categories

The broad idea:

Sell the right insurance to the customer, not simply the product that pays the most commission.

📉 SO WHY DID INSURANCE STOCKS FALL?

Because the market immediately started calculating:

“If commissions fall → distributor income falls → earnings could fall.”

🔴 Insurance distributors

Stocks such as PB Fintech (Policybazaar) and Turtlemint were among the more heavily impacted.

Their business models are closely connected to insurance distribution economics.

Some analysts estimated that even a 10% reduction in commissions could have a meaningful impact on earnings, depending on the company’s product mix.

🔴 Insurance companies

Several life and general insurers also fell, including names such as:

HDFC Life
ICICI Prudential Life
Max Financial
SBI Life
Star Health
ICICI Lombard
LIC

Why?

Because lower expense limits + lower upfront commissions could affect:

➡️ Distribution costs
➡️ New business growth
➡️ Margins
➡️ Incentives to sell certain products

🔴 Banks & NBFCs

Banks and lenders also came under pressure.

Why?

Because bancassurance and credit-linked insurance generate fee income.

If commissions on these products are sharply reduced and compulsory bundling is restricted that income stream could be affected.

Policybazaar Shares Fall 26% on IRDAI Proposals

Policybazaar parent PB Fintech shares came under heavy selling pressure, falling around 26%, after IRDAI proposed a wide-ranging overhaul of insurance distribution economics.

Proposed Changes to Insurance Commissions:
IRDAI's consultation paper proposes linking distributor commissions to factors including product complexity, distribution channel, policy size and selling effort.
For health insurance, the proposal includes commission limits of 15%–20% for new policies, while renewal and portability commissions could be capped at lower levels. Motor and life insurance commissions would also face proposed product-specific limits.

Why Policybazaar Is in Focus:
Policybazaar operates primarily as an online insurance distribution platform, making the proposed commission framework particularly relevant to its business economics.
According to Jefferies, a 10% reduction in commission rates could potentially translate into a 10%–12% decline in earnings for PB Fintech and Turtlemint. This is a brokerage estimate, not a confirmed impact.

IRDAI Also Targets Distribution Costs:
The regulator has proposed a five-year reduction in Expense of Management limits, alongside greater disclosure of commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.

The proposals also include restrictions on volume-linked incentives, commission clawbacks in cases of mis-selling, and greater use of digital infrastructure such as Bima Sugam.

The consultation process is currently open, with stakeholders invited to submit comments by October 25, 2026. These are proposals and are not yet final regulations.

#Insurance #PolicyBazar #PBfintech #NSE
@Prakashplutus Policybazaar turtlemint

Banks earn serious money selling policies. In FY26, HDFC Bank made around Rs 57bn in life insurance commissions alone. Axis Bank about Rs 32bn. SBI roughly Rs 24bn.

Not law. Not final. Not effective tomorrow.

⚠️ Point 2: Impact ≠ Uniform
- Bancassurance-heavy insurers (SBI Life, HDFC Life) less exposed
- Online aggregators (PB Fintech) MOST exposed
- Traditional agent-driven insurers (LIC) least exposed
The market dumped all of them equally today.
That's a mispricing signal — not a fact.

This is not a buy list.

High relative strength can indicate that a stock is outperforming its benchmark, but momentum can also reverse sharply. Current screening methodologies similarly caution that technical strength should be combined with trend, volume and risk controls.

Study. Track. Research. Don't blindly follow.

Digital personal-loan platforms have made applications faster and more convenient, but the rate shown in an advertisement is generally a starting/indicative rate—not necessarily the rate every borrower will receive. 🔎 What borrowers should compare

Looking only at the headline interest rate can be misleading. Before accepting a personal loan, compare:

Annual interest rate / APR

Processing fee

GST and other applicable charges

Prepayment / foreclosure charges

Late-payment and penal charges

Loan tenure

Total repayment / EMI

Actual lender behind the app

Paisabazaar's current September 2026 information also notes that processing fees, foreclosure/prepayment charges, part-payment charges, late-payment penalties and other applicable charges may affect the overall cost of a personal loan. 

⚠️ Important digital-lending check

The RBI advises borrowers to verify that a digital lending app is associated with an RBI-regulated bank/NBFC or its authorised Lending Service Provider (LSP). RBI guidance also requires regulated digital-lending arrangements to disclose the loan's Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and certain other costs and data practices. 

So, “instant” doesn't automatically mean “cheap.” The actual cost of credit and the regulated lender behind the app matter.

🚨 Big investment incoming in Haldia!!

Another major industrial proposal is taking shape in Haldia, with the Saroj Poddar Group planning a new phosphatic fertiliser plant with an investment of around ₹2,000 crore.

🔹 Investment: ~₹2,000 crore
🔹 Land requirement: 100–150 acres
🔹 Location: Haldia, Purba Medinipur
🔹 Sector: Phosphatic fertilisers
🔹 Raw material: Rock phosphate to be imported from Morocco
🔹 Key requirement: Direct port connectivity.

The group had EARLIER CONSIDERED a 1-million-tonne fertiliser plant in KARNATAKA, but is now planning two plants — one in Bengal and another elsewhere — with a combined investment of around ₹4,000 crore.

According to the group, Bengal currently lacks a major phosphatic fertiliser manufacturing unit, creating a supply gap that the proposed Haldia facility could help address.

💰 AND THIS ISN'T THE ONLY INVESTMENT

The Saroj Poddar Group says it plans to invest ₹10,000–11,000 crore in Bengal over the next 3–4 years.
It is also developing a 100-acre logistics & warehousing park at Sankrail, Howrah, involving an investment of around ₹1,000 crore.

Industrial confidence is returning under the new government.

Riding the Infrastructure Wave: Unlocking Man Industries' Multi-Year Growth Blueprint

The global line pipe sector is undergoing a massive structural shift. Driven by intense energy security mandates in the Middle East and heavy public utility outlays in India, Man Industries (India) Ltd. has repositioned itself from a standard regional exporter into a localized, cross-border manufacturing platform.

This breakdown covers the physical capacities, structural value-mix changes, long-term valuation modeling, and the future growth opportunities for Man Industries up to FY32 and beyond.

Scaling the Factory Floors: Capacity & Revenue Ceilings

Historically, Man Industries operated a baseline capacity of 1.20 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA), heavily centered on standard carbon steel submerged arc welded (SAW) pipes in India. Under this legacy setup, pricing limits and competitive domestic bidding restricted the absolute revenue ceiling to roughly ₹4,500 – ₹4,800 Crores.

Following the acquisition of Saudi Arabia's National Pipe Company (NPC) and key infrastructure expansions, the global operational blueprint scales to 1.63 Million MTPA. More importantly, the company is optimizing this total tonnage across premium nodes:

1. The Jammu Greenfield Plant: A specialized facility adding 22,000 MTPA of high-margin Stainless Steel Seamless Pipes and Tubes, targeted for full commercialization by early FY28.

2. The Dammam Coating Node: A localized value-added coating plant in Saudi Arabia that shifts production from bare pipes to insulated, high-yield anti-corrosion lines.

The Capital Result: By shifting production toward higher-priced stainless steel and integrated pipe coating systems, the company's maximum physical revenue potential expands to a ceiling of ₹11,500 Crores at peak optimal utilization.

Increasing capacity utilizations over next 5 years: 

Management has provided near-term guidance of ₹5,000 – ₹5,500 Crores in revenue for FY27, backed by an explicit projection of 25% to 35% growth in FY28. Over the long term, the company aims to move utilization up to its absolute physical cap.

Assuming a 20% CAGR in revenues over next 5 years backed by a stable 15% margins (due to premium product mix), reducing finance cost, we can expect a EPS CAGR of 25-30%. 

Order Book Backbone Needed to Match This Growth 

To support this upward trajectory, the underlying order engine must expand to ensure execution visibility:

Current Backlog: The company holds a solid ₹3,600 Crore order book, backed by a massive ₹24,000 Crore bidding pipeline (70% focused in the high-yield MENA region).

FY32 Required Backlog: To reliably sustain a manufacturing output of ₹11,500 Crores, the rolling order book needs to scale to a steady baseline of ₹8,500 – ₹9,500 Crores, requiring a global active bidding pool that continuously hovers around ₹45,000 Crores.

Breaking the Ceiling: Post-FY32 Growth Opportunities

Once Man Industries hits 100% capacity utilization at its ₹11,500 Crore ceiling, it cannot grow further through standard domestic volume scaling. Post-FY32, the company's next phase of growth will likely shift to non-volume levers to capitalize on secular tailwinds:

1. Pure Pricing Power & Alloy Premiumization

Even with a fixed volume of 1.63 Million MTPA, the company can mix-shift its output toward high-value Corrosion Resistant Alloy (CRA) lined pipes used for deep-water and highly sour gas fields. This transition shifts the growth driver from volume to value, supporting a steady 3% to 5% price-led organic revenue CAGR.

2. Service-Heavy "Coating-Only" Revenue Mix

Instead of acting purely as a steel processor, the company can utilize the specialized Dammam Coating Facility to coat bare line pipes manufactured by third parties. Because this model excludes the pass-through cost of raw steel plates, it expands corporate margins toward 18–20%, generating substantial cash flow with minimal extra capital requirements.

3. Launching Phase 3 Global Capex Modules

By FY32, the business will be highly deleveraged, generating significant free cash flow. This financial flexibility position allows management to launch a Phase 3 Greenfield module—potentially establishing localized ERW/SAW manufacturing hubs in emerging infrastructure areas like North Africa or the Americas, structurally lifting the revenue ceiling past ₹15,000+ Crores.

4. Capturing the Transnational Hydrogen Pipeline Shift

The global pivot toward green hydrogen requires high-pressure, zero-permeability pipeline networks. Man Industries' early move into certified metallurgy positions them to capture these high-margin, specialized infrastructure allocations as global utilities begin updating their networks over the coming decade.

Summary: Core Investor Takeaways & Valuation Triggers

For Man Industries to maintain its valuation and capture long-term upside, it must achieve three core operational triggers:

1. Structural ROE Improvement: The business must move away from historical 9–10% ROEs to stabilize within the 18–20% bracket. This requires the high-margin Jammu Stainless Steel and Saudi Dammam Coating lines to operate at high utilization while cash flows from Merino Shelters help pay down peak debt.

2. Scaled Order Book Backlog: The current ₹3,600 Crore backlog only secures short-term targets. To sustain its 5-year growth path toward peak capacity, the company must convert its ₹24,000 Crore MENA bid pipeline to maintain a rolling order book of ₹8,500 – ₹9,500 Crores.

3. Phase 3 Capex Announcements: Current projects cap the ultimate revenue potential at a hard ceiling of ₹11,500 Crores. Announcing a Phase 3 Greenfield module using generated free cash flow would lift this ceiling and provide a major valuation rerate by extending the volume growth phase.
